title: Per-customer & per-route policy playbook: safe apply, canary simulation, and automatic rollback
creator: Maya Tran
description: Define and implement an operational playbook and automation for applying per-customer and per-route optimization policies (batching/caching, allowlists/denylists, tier affinity) with strong safety controls: offline validation, canary dry-run, traffic-gradual canary, metrics-driven rollback, and audit loggable actions. Goal: reduce token cost by safely enabling more aggressive batching/caching rules while preserving latency SLOs and output quality.
acceptance_criteria: Policy author can run a dry-run simulator that replays 7 days of real traffic and produces cost delta / latency delta / model mismatch risk report
A new 'Policy Delta Preview' UI panel is available in Console for per-route and per-customer policies showing expected cost savings and risk bands
Safe-apply orchestration supports staged canary by traffic fraction (e.g., 1%, 5%, 25%) with automatic roll-forward or rollback rules based on configurable indicators
Automated rollback triggers if key metrics degrade beyond thresholds for 3 consecutive minutes: latency_p95 increase > 15% AND model_mismatch_rate increase > 0.5% OR error_rate increase > 0.2%
All policy changes (dry-run, canary start/end, rollbacks) are recorded with immutable audit entries and linked to the initiating user/PR
Migration path for legacy policy schema to new rule scaffold without downtime
technical_notes: Introduce Policy Delta Previewer: offline simulator that consumes anonymized prefix tokens, KV cache patterns and route metadata to estimate batching hit-rate and cache efficacy
Simulator uses stratified sampling per-customer route: heavy, medium, light traffic buckets to avoid biasing results by spikes
Implement staged-apply orchestrator service (policy-orch) that manages canary fractions, snapshotting current runtime config, and applying deltas via compatibility-checked delta patches
Runtime compatibility checks: ensure kernel/quantization variant compatibility between fallback and target models; reject applies where sequence-length distribution mismatch > 2x
Add a 'safety clamp' to runtime scheduler: limit aggregator window growth per-route during canary to avoid sudden batching-induced latency spikes
Expose telemetry events: policy.apply.start, policy.apply.step, policy.apply.rollback, policy.simulate.report with trace IDs
Use existing SLO/alerting infra; create new metrics: policy_cost_savings_estimate, policy_simulated_latency_p95, policy_model_mismatch_rate
Security: require SSO + allowlist for users initiating production applies; record signed commit in audit log (KMS-backed)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Spec + UI mockups (this ticket): finalize acceptance criteria and safety thresholds
Phase 1 - Simulator service and cost/latency report prototype; run internal sims against historical traces (infra staging)
Phase 2 - Policy Delta Preview UI in Console (read-only) and CLI dry-run command
Phase 3 - Staged-apply orchestrator with canary fractions and telemetry hooks; gated behind feature flag
Phase 4 - Integration tests + chaos tests (inject latency, drop responses) and run canary on internal customers
Phase 5 - Soft launch: opt-in beta with 3 pilot customers; monitor for 2 weeks
Phase 6 - General availability and deprecation plan for legacy policy endpoints
telemetry_and_safety_checks: Primary indicators: latency_p95 (route), avg_token_cost_per_1k, error_rate, model_mismatch_rate (structured output divergence)
Canary aggregation window: 5 minutes with 1-minute resolution. Require stable signals for 3 windows before roll-forward
Automated rollback policy: strict AND/OR combination of indicators to prevent noisy single-metric rollbacks
Shadow mode: feed a mirrored subset of traffic to the candidate policy path and compare outputs; use divergence scorer (Levenshtein/structured-field mismatch)
Telemetry retention for sim reports: 90 days. Audit trails for production applies retained for 1 year
Alerts: immediate Slack + PagerDuty if rollbacks triggered for pilot customers or high-tier accounts
